summary: António de Oliveira Salazar (1889–1970), a professor of finance at Coimbra, entered the Military Dictatorship's government as finance minister in 1928 with a veto over all public spending, became President of the Council in 1932, and wrote the constitution that founded the Estado Novo in 1933. He governed for thirty-six years: austere public finances, corporatism, censorship, a political police, no legal opposition, neutrality in the world war combined with the Azores concession to the Allies, NATO in 1949, and from 1961 a refusal to decolonise that committed the country to war on three fronts. Historians differ over whether the regime is best described as fascist or as conservative Catholic authoritarianism, and over how much of its longevity was his own doing. Incapacitated in 1968, he was replaced without being informed and died in 1970 believing he still governed. He is in the atlas as the actor most of the twentieth-century Portuguese chains pass through.
